WHO THIS IS FOR
Prabhavit Gupta, Venice, Italy. Indian passport with an Italian EU long-term residence permit, so he works across most of the EU with no sponsorship. Ireland and Denmark opted out of that directive; the UK, Switzerland and the US need sponsorship, so tag those companies freelance-only. About 3 years experience.
Most recently FlowSpace, a coworking-space booking platform grown from 2,000 to 4,500+ users, where he built AI support agents, lead capture and enrichment into the CRM, outbound and sales-funnel automation, and a scraping and parsing pipeline. He led a Bubble.io to Next.js and Laravel migration on that live product.
Stack: n8n (deep: agentic workflows, human-in-the-loop steps, tool definitions, retries, error handling), OpenAI and Anthropic APIs, Make, Zapier, Airtable, Next.js, React, TypeScript, Node.js, Laravel and PHP, Supabase, Postgres, REST APIs and webhooks, Microsoft Copilot Studio and Power Automate (certified).
English only, no working Italian, German, French or Dutch. Targets EUR 30,000-40,000 salary, or EUR 200 a day as an Italian sole trader with an individual Partita IVA. He has NO limited company, so skip anyone who contracts only with limited companies.

TAG EVERY COMPANY with one or both modes:
- "speculative job": his profile fits well enough that a direct approach could surface or create a role.
- "freelance client": they would plausibly BUY n8n / AI automation / integration work from him at around EUR 200 a day. EUR 200/day is well under typical EU agency rates, which is his main selling point.

YOUR LANE: the automation delivery economy in Europe. Cover:
1. n8n's own partner and expert ecosystem: agencies and consultancies listed as n8n partners, n8n Experts, or that publicly market themselves as n8n implementation shops in the EU.
2. Make.com and Zapier solution partners and certified partners based in the EU.
3. EU AI-automation and AI-agent agencies and studios that build for clients: the kind that post case studies about workflow automation, AI agents, RAG chatbots or GTM automation.
4. GTM engineering and RevOps agencies in the EU that build Clay, HubSpot, Apollo and outbound automation for clients.
5. European AI consultancies and digital product studios that would subcontract automation work.
Prioritise companies that are small to mid size, EU-based, work in English, and visibly take on client projects. A company that publishes case studies or a "work with us" or "become a partner" page is a better target than a large consultancy.

FOR EACH COMPANY RETURN
- what they do, one line
- the SPECIFIC reason he is worth their time, tied to something real he built. His differentiators: he has shipped n8n agentic workflows with human-in-the-loop and retry logic in production rather than demo automations; he can also write the app around the automation in Next.js, React and Laravel, which most automation freelancers cannot; and at EUR 200 a day he is well below EU agency contractor rates.
- best route in. He will message people on LinkedIn, so give the exact JOB TITLE to search for at that company plus the company LinkedIn URL. Name a person ONLY if their name and role are published on the company's own website or a press page, and say where you saw it. NEVER invent or guess a person or an email address. If they publish a general contact, careers, or partner email on their own site, quote it verbatim. If they have a "work with us as a freelancer" or partner-application page, give that URL, since that is a better route than a cold message.
- what he should lead with, one concrete sentence.
- watch-outs: language, whether they need a limited company, whether they are really a staffing body shop, whether they look dormant.

RULES
- The company must currently exist and look active. Verify the site and LinkedIn are live.
- NO em dashes or en dashes anywhere. Plain hyphens only.
- Never invent a URL, person, email or funding figure. If unknown write "not stated".
- Do NOT return these, already covered as live job leads: n8n itself, Make and Celonis, Zapier, Lleverage.ai, GTM Base, SalesCaptain, Huzzle, Sophie.camp, Paires, Swans, 10x.Team, Dorado Software Group, TripleTen, Wing Assistant, INFUSE, Pavago, Intellectsoft, Toptal, A.Team, Talent Sam, Jobgether.

OUTPUT: ONLY a JSON array, no prose:
{"company":"","what":"","hq":"","size":"","mode":"speculative job|freelance client|both","why_him":"","route_in":"","linkedin":"","public_email":"","lead_with":"","watch_outs":"","source":""}
Aim for 14 to 18 companies.

Outbound HTTPS from this session goes through a local proxy at http://127.0.0.1:39729
(set via HTTPS_PROXY) which tunnels to a policy-enforcing egress proxy. TLS is
re-terminated there, so every tool must trust the CA bundle at
/root/.ccr/ca-bundle.crt. The standard CA environment variables, the system trust
store (where possible), a JVM truststore, the Bazel system bazelrc, the
browser NSS store, and gsutil's boto config are already set up.

## Quick diagnosis

1. Run: curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:39729/__agentproxy/status
   It reports proxy state, which trust and git accommodations are active
   (javaTrustStorePath, toolTrustFailureCodes, gitSshRewrite,
   gitConfigConflicts), and the most recent proxy-side failures.
2. Find the failure class below and apply the matching fix; gitConfigConflicts
   codes map to the git section, toolTrustFailureCodes to the JVM section.
3. Never disable TLS verification, never unset HTTPS_PROXY, and do not retry
   organization policy denials (403/407) — report them instead.

## Failure classes and fixes

### "certificate verify failed" / "self-signed certificate in chain" / PKIX errors

The failing tool is not reading the pre-set CA configuration. In order:

- If the tool has a CA flag or env var, point it at /root/.ccr/ca-bundle.crt
  (examples: --cacert, SSL_CERT_FILE, NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS, REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE,
  AWS_CA_BUNDLE, DENO_CERT, CARGO_HTTP_CAINFO, PIP_CERT, GIT_SSL_CAINFO,
  BUNDLE_SSL_CA_CERT, HEX_CACERTS_PATH, NIX_SSL_CERT_FILE).
- Tool config files override environment variables. If one of these sets its
  own CA or disables verification, point it at the bundle instead:
  pip.conf "cert", npm "cafile" (npm config get cafile), ~/.curlrc "cacert",
  .wgetrc "ca_certificate", conda "ssl_verify", git "http.sslCAInfo",
  gradle.properties / MAVEN_OPTS "-Djavax.net.ssl.trustStore".
- JVM tools (Maven, Gradle, plain Java): when a JDK is present, a truststore
  is built at /root/.ccr/java-truststore.p12 (password "changeit") and
  injected via JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS — confirm javaTrustStorePath is set in the
  status output before pointing a build at it (toolTrustFailureCodes explains
  why it is missing). If the image or the build sets its own trustStore, that
  one wins — import the proxy CA into it with
  keytool -importcert -noprompt -alias ccr-agent-proxy -file /root/.ccr/agent-proxy-ca.crt -keystore <their store>
  or point the build at the ready-made one. Bazel reads the managed block in
  /etc/bazel.bazelrc rather than JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS.

### "405 Method Not Allowed" from the proxy

The tool sent a plain-HTTP (non-CONNECT) request: usually axios older than
1.16.1 (upgrade it) or a tool configured with HTTP_PROXY (unset HTTP_PROXY for
that tool — only HTTPS_PROXY is supported).

### 403 / 407 from the proxy

The destination host is not allowed by your organization's egress policy for
this session. Do not retry or route around it — report the blocked host.
Note: curl hides response bodies on failed CONNECTs; the status endpoint
records the reason.

Some clients do not read HTTPS_PROXY: Node's built-in fetch (run that command
